summary: Protect freshly spot-seeded patches and let the cut lawn regrow. Check moisture rather than relying on watering minutes alone.

cards.name: New rye lawn
cards.action: Keep fresh repair seed moist without puddles or runoff. Let the cut grass regrow and avoid mowing or raking newly seeded patches. A possibly low cut does not by itself confirm damage.
cards.amount: Current reported setting: 3 minutes per run. This is not a calibrated watering depth; check that all repaired areas actually get wet and remain moist until the next run.
cards.frequency: Current reported setting: four runs daily. Use for repair germination only as needed for moisture; skip already-wet runs. After repairs establish, gradually reduce frequency and water more deeply rather than keeping four daily pulses indefinitely.
cards.nextCheck: Check repaired patches for first sprouts around November 18. Report earlier emergence when observed; do not restart the original lawn’s timeline.
cards.why: Older rye and newly sown repair seed are at different growth stages. Short pulses suit a germinating seedbed but may not meet the older grass’s developing root-zone needs.

cards.name: Green hopseed
cards.action: Check moisture inside the original root ball daily. Hand-water slowly when it begins drying, keeping it moist rather than soggy.
cards.amount: Wet the root ball and nearby soil; an exact volume needs a moisture and delivery check.
cards.frequency: Continue daily moisture checks during establishment; watering remains conditional. Do not change the shared valve schedule before checking emitter delivery and soil.
cards.nextCheck: Drip readiness check due: report whether the root ball is moist or drying and identify emitter GPH and count.
cards.why: New shrub roots need reliable moisture. Nursery container size is not a watering dose.

cards.name: Barrel & totem cactus
cards.status: Cool-season care · allow drying between waterings
cards.action: End the first-week daily hose routine. Use targeted manual watering when the root-area soil has dried, with no additional drip run. Check beneath the gravel rather than judging from the dry surface alone.
cards.amount: Gently wet the root area without flooding it or keeping the cactus stem wet. Hose flow is unmeasured, so 30 seconds is not a calibrated amount.
cards.frequency: Starting plan: roughly once every two weeks after the last actual watering, only if soil is dry. Check moisture weekly; defer while damp or after effective rain. Reassess if the nursery root ball dries much faster.
cards.nextCheck: Confirm the last actual watering day to set the next check date. Do not water solely because the calendar interval has elapsed.
cards.why: Cool-season cactus roots use water slowly. The soil must dry between waterings; an automatic daily or twice-weekly shared drip schedule can keep it wet.

cards.name: Moroccan mound
cards.action: Keep it on a separate low-water approach from the hopseed. Let soil dry between waterings.
cards.amount: Avoid saturating the root area repeatedly; exact delivery is not yet calibrated.
cards.frequency: Check soil first; no automatic extra hand-watering while wet.
cards.nextCheck: Review soil moisture before connecting it to a frequent shared drip schedule.
cards.why: This is a succulent, not a shrub that should stay steadily moist.

cards.name: Hybrid fan & Mediterranean fan palms
cards.action: Check root-zone moisture before a drip run. Do not increase watering simply because new plants were added.
cards.amount: Recorded baseline: about 24 gallons per palm per run; this has not been validated against root-zone wetting.
cards.frequency: Recorded baseline: about every four days. Skip or adjust when soil is already wet.
cards.nextCheck: Check the root area before the next scheduled run.
cards.why: Emitter flow controls volume, but every plant on a valve shares its watering days.

tasks.title: First rye fertilizer
tasks.instruction: Original lawn’s planned first feeding: 1.54 lb total of plain Scotts Starter 24-25-4 with listed drop setting 6 subject to bag/model. Recheck the mixed-age lawn before application, since repair seed was sown later. Do not add extra fertilizer to compensate for a low cut or repeat starter already used at seeding.

tasks.title: Repair seed germination
tasks.instruction: Keep repair seed moist without saturation and protect it from traffic or mowing. Check for first sprouts around November 18 and report earlier emergence if observed. Older rye and repair seedlings have different timelines; do not automatically add more seed or another starter feeding.

tasks.title: New plant drip review
tasks.instruction: Check hopseed root-ball moisture and identify its emitter count and GPH before moving to drip. Do not switch all plants to twice-weekly watering automatically. Assess cacti and Moroccan mound separately; keep cactus drip off if using hand-watering.
tasks.when: Due now · root moisture and emitter check

tasks.title: Next mowing after regrowth
tasks.instruction: First mowing is confirmed; cut height is unknown. Allow new rye to regrow toward about 2¾–3 inches, then use a sharp rotary blade around 2½ inches on dry grass and firm ground. Avoid freshly seeded repair patches until their seedlings are rooted and tall enough.
